design_gate_result.dominant_error_mode: keyword-latching: process-NAME words appearing as noun-modifiers or in unrelated senses ('combustion engine', 'fossil fuel', 'radioactive decay', 'chemical condensation', 'carbon dioxide') get tagged as that process even when the entity-fate event is a different (or no) process.

final_verdict_msg: HARD_FAIL (PARTIAL BOOTSTRAP: reading EXTENDS but the seed must permanently carry process-precision). DESIGN GATE: process-tag accuracy (hand-checked) = 0.7167 (86/120), at/below the 0.7 gate -- reading cannot RELIABLY identify the process (dominant error = keyword-latching on process-name words in unrelated contexts: {'combustion': 5, 'water_cycle': 5, 'digestion': 5, 'carbon_cycle': 4, 'fossilization': 4, 'respiration': 4, 'photosynthesis': 3, 'electricity_generation': 2, 'erosion_weathering': 2}). SEPARATELY + decisively, COVERAGE COLLAPSE: 86% of fate-facts (3326/3888) were SKIPPED because the sentence states the entity-fate but carries NO taggable process signal -> reading yield fell from ~3817 (entity-global v1) to 562 tagged facts. RESULT: process-keyed reading_only recall = 0.0968 (rises from 0.0323 but saturates LOW), seed_only=0.2097, combined=0.2419; LESION gap=0.1451 (>> 0.05, does NOT fade), OVERLAP=0.3077 (4/13); SCRAMBLE retained=0.6663 (small-N noise on a low base). CONCLUSION: matching reading to the seed's PROCESS-KEYED grain does NOT let the crutch fade, because (a) science prose rarely co-states entity-fate AND an unambiguous process, and (b) glass-box process-tagging is only ~0.7167 accurate (keyword-latching). The bootstrap is EXTEND-NOT-FULLY-FADE: reading grows the store (entity-global, validated) but the hand-vetted seed must PERMANENTLY supply process-conditioned precision -- an honest, conclusive limit of no-LLM grow-by-reading on this task.
